title: Annotatio V §.XII (4) replies: anger makes testimony stronger; Bucer; Chytraeus Marburg
pass_a_gloss: Reply (1.) Luther’s Testimony is so much the more excellent and efficacious as it proceeded more from Luther angry at the Zwinglians. (2.) Luther’s anger was not so turned against the Zwinglian Negation of Oral Eating as against a hypothesis anger imputed to them, never cherished by them — as if in the Holy Supper nothing but bread and wine were had — which Bucer six hundred times showed Luther in his English Writings. (3.) At Marburg it was not so agreed as the Author reports from Luther’s Epistle to the Provost, but as Chytraeus reports in the History of the Augustan Confession, whose words cited more than once run: Although whether Christ’s true body and Blood be CORPORALLY present in the bread and wine of the Lord’s Supper we have not this time agreed: Yet ONE PART will declare Christian love to THE OTHER, and BOTH PARTS will diligently pray almighty God that HE confirm US by his Spirit in the true opinion, Amen.
pass_b_english: Replies: (1) testimony from an angry Luther is stronger, not weaker; (2) the anger aimed less at denying Oral than at the false charge that the Supper is only bread and wine — which Bucer proved false to Luther many times in the English writings.

(3) Marburg’s terms are Chytraeus’s, not the Author’s Provost-letter version: they had not agreed whether body and blood are corporally present, yet each side would show Christian love and both would pray for the Spirit’s confirmation. Amen.
source_text: Resp. (1.) Testimonium Lutheri tantò præstantius esse & efficacius, quantò magis ab irascente Zwinglianis Luthero profectum est. (2.) Lutheri iram non adeò versam fuisse in Oralis Manducationis Negationem Zwinglianam, quàm in hypothesin, per iram, Zwinglianis imputatam, ab his verò fotam nunquam, quasi in S. Cœna nil nisi panis & vinum habeatur, id quod sexcenties Bucerus Luthero demonstravit in Scriptis suis Anglicis. (3.) Marpurgi non ita conventum esse, ut Autor refert ex Epistola Lutheri ad Præpositum, sed ut Chytræus refert in Hist. August. Confessionis, cujus verba plus semel citata ita habent: Etsi verò an verum corpus & Sanguis Christi CORPORALITER in pane & vino Cœnæ Domini præsens sit, hoc tempore non concordavimus: Tamen UNA PARS ALTERI Christianam dilectionem declarabit, & UTRAQUE PARS Deum omnipotentem diligenter orabit, ut NOS Spiritu suo in vera sententia confirmet, Amen.
